title: CPU stage placement classes
description: Named placement classes for CPU-only scientific stages. Several Terraform owners contribute class entries; modules/kueue-scheduling is the sole assembler and emits the merged map as cpu_classes inside the content-addressed kueue-scheduling.json ConfigMap. There is one schema, one assembled document, and one key. A CPU stage receives no accelerator ResourceFlavor, so it inherits no node labels and no tolerations; on a tainted pool it would never schedule. Each class therefore carries its own queue identity, node routing, tolerations, per-node capacity, the cpu/memory ResourceFlavor its admissions report, the pools it may land on, and how the pool it actually landed on is determined. A class absent from the assembled map means that placement is not deployed, never that a stage may fall back to another class.

cpu_classes.description: Class ID to placement. Keys are stable and stage-facing: a stage names the class it needs and a consumer freezes that class per stage rather than applying one global CPU placement. A class is bound to exactly one namespace, so a producer that runs the same lane in several namespaces contributes one class per namespace.

class_id.description: Four class IDs are defined by this version. 'reference-data' is the tainted pool that mounts the shared reference databases in the academic namespace beside AlphaFold 3's raw data stage. 'model-reference-data' is the same storage-attached backing reached through a distinct LocalQueue in the ordinary model namespace. 'general-cpu' is untainted general capacity in the ordinary model namespace. 'academic-cpu' is the same general CPU backing reached through a distinct LocalQueue in the academic claim namespace, currently for BindCraft aggregation. Any other ID is producer-defined and a consumer must treat it as unknown rather than as a synonym for one of these.

quantity.description: An apimachinery resource.Quantity exactly as the producer observed it on the Node, so a consumer can compare against a Pod request without a lossy round trip through an integer.

local_queue.description: LocalQueue a stage of this class is submitted to. Its identity is the (namespace, local_queue) pair: consumers that key LocalQueues by bare name cannot represent the same name in two namespaces, so the assembler refuses a name reused across classes.

cluster_queue.description: ClusterQueue that admits it, which must admit this class's namespace. It may be owned by a different Terraform configuration than the one that contributes this class.

namespace.description: The one namespace this class runs in. A licensed claim can only be mounted from its own namespace, so this is not always the model namespace.

resource_flavor.description: ResourceFlavor a cpu/memory admission of this class reports in status.admission.podSetAssignments[*].flavors. It verifies the flavor frozen for this class and identifies node placement, not the class by itself: namespace-specific classes may share one ResourceFlavor when their ClusterQueue, pool resolution, selectors, tolerations, and capacity are identical. See pool_resolution for actual pool identity.

eligible_pool_ids.description: Every pool a stage of this class may land on. This is the expected set, not the outcome. A consumer records it as expected_eligible_pool_ids and must never present it as the pool the stage actually ran on.

pool_resolution.description: How the pool a stage actually landed on is determined. Kueue reports a ResourceFlavor, not a pool, so a class whose one flavor spans several pools cannot answer this from the admission alone.

mode.description: 'per-pool-flavor': the class has one eligible pool and its ResourceFlavor names that pool, so the admission determines it. 'node-label-observation': one flavor spans several pools, so the actual pool is only knowable after scheduling, by reading node_label_key from the assigned Node.

pool_id.description: Required and equal to the single eligible pool when mode is per-pool-flavor. Forbidden otherwise, because an optional pool ID beside a multi-pool flavor reads as an assignment that was never made.

node_label_key.description: Required when mode is node-label-observation: the Node label carrying the pool ID, read from the Node the Pod was scheduled onto. Forbidden otherwise.

node_selector.description: Node labels the stage Pod must carry to land on this class's capacity. Required and non-empty: no accelerator ResourceFlavor supplies them, so a class with no selector routes nowhere in particular.

tolerations.description: Tolerations the stage Pod must carry. Required, and an empty array is the correct value for untainted capacity: stating no tolerations is different from omitting the field.

schedulable_capacity.description: Measured per-node allocatable capacity, not a preset's nominal size, in one canonical representation: cpu is exactly the millicore integer with an 'm' suffix, memory and ephemeral_storage are exactly the MiB integers with a 'Mi' suffix. The quantity and the integer are the same number in two spellings, so a consumer may read either and they can never disagree. The assembler rejects a mismatch. A stage whose largest Pod exceeds this can never be scheduled, so a renderer refuses the plan rather than queueing it forever. The smallest node in the class is the honest value when the class spans several pools.

ephemeral_storage_mib.description: Zero means the pool advertises no ephemeral storage budget, which is different from a pool that advertises some.

pool_id.description: An accelerator-pool-contract pool ID. The same grammar the scheduling module accepts: a lowercase Kubernetes label value of at most 63 characters, so dots and underscores that appear in real pool IDs are legal. Deliberately wider than a DNS label, because pool IDs are label values, not object names.

qualified_name.description: A Kubernetes qualified name: an optional DNS-subdomain prefix of at most 253 characters, a slash, and a name of at most 63, so at most 317 in total. The lookahead bounds the prefix on its own; a total-length rule alone would accept a 254-character prefix beside a short name, which the API rejects.
